# Agent Memory Design Guide

> A short, vendor-neutral guide to structuring persistent memory for AI
> agents: what to write, how to organize it, when to delete it, and how
> to keep retrieved memory from being treated as instructions. Applies to
> any storage backend and any agent framework.

This repository is a design guide, not a library or SDK; there's no code
to install. It's meant to be read by both humans and coding agents, and
applied when designing or reviewing an agent's memory system.

## Core guide

- [README.md](README.md): The guide itself. Six practices: namespace by
  kind, one fact per write, gate every write, plan for forgetting, treat
  memory as data not instructions, and document your scheme, each with a
  short rationale. Ends with a copy-paste template for documenting a
  memory scheme.

## Review

- [checklist.md](checklist.md): 12 yes/no questions for auditing an
  existing memory system against the guide, 2 per section of the README.

## Examples

- [examples/01-namespacing-and-atomic-writes.md](examples/01-namespacing-and-atomic-writes.md):
  A worked customer-support session showing the difference between one
  bundled summary write and 3 correctly namespaced atomic writes.
- [examples/02-gating-writes.md](examples/02-gating-writes.md): 3
  candidate writes from one session evaluated against the importance,
  dedup, and secret checks, including a payment credential that must be
  rejected outright.
- [examples/03-forgetting-and-injection.md](examples/03-forgetting-and-injection.md):
  A memory-injection attempt through an ordinary chat message, a
  right-to-be-forgotten deletion request, and a supersession example
  showing how an updated fact should replace an old one.

## Applying this guide

- [SKILL.md](SKILL.md): Instructions for a coding agent on how to apply
  this guide when designing or reviewing a memory system. Read this if
  you're an agent being asked to do that work, not a human reading the
  guide directly.
